title: Enforcement Rules of the Management of the National Funds Act
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters delegated by the Management of the National Funds Act and its Enforcement Decree and matters necessary for their enforcement. <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in these Rules mean the following: <Amended 2005.6.30>
1. “Public officials engaged in accounting” means revenue collection officers, finance officers, disbursing officers, officers authorizing transactions in funds for advance use, cashiers and persons acting in all or separately undertaking part of their affairs under Article 40 of the Management of the National Funds Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”);
2. “Accounting books” means receipts collection ledgers prepared by revenue collection officers, commitment-to-disburse ledgers prepared by finance officers, disbursements ledgers prepared by disbursing officers, and cash transaction ledgers prepared by cashiers under Article 92 of the Enforcement Decree of the Management of the National Funds Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Decree”).

Article 3 (Scope of Application)
(1) Except as otherwise specifically provided by other statutes or regulations, public officials engaged in accounting shall handle their affairs as prescribed by these Rules.
(2) Except as otherwise specifically provided by other statutes or regulations, the Bank of Korea and treasury banks (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank of Korea, etc.”), and financial companies, etc. under Article 11(2) of the Decree (hereinafter referred to as “financial companies, etc.”), shall handle transactions in national funds as prescribed by these Rules. <Amended 2011.10.4>

CHAPTER II RECEIPTS

SECTION 1 COLLECTION DETERMINATIONS

Article 4 (Collection Determinations) Where an amount must be collected as receipts, or notification thereof is received, under statutes or regulations or a contract (hereinafter referred to as “statutes, etc.”) or for other reasons, the revenue collection officer shall investigate the following matters, determine its collection as receipts using the Receipts Collection Resolution in attached Form 1, and record it in the Receipts Collection Ledger in attached Form 2: <Amended 2005.6.30, 2007.11.6, 2013.6.28>
1. Basis for the receipt;
2. Name and address of the taxpayer, etc.;
3. Real-name identification number of the taxpayer, etc. (meaning a resident registration number, business registration number or unique identification number under Article 12(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act; hereinafter the same applies);
4. Amount payable and basis for its calculation;
5. Payment deadline;
6. Fiscal year to which it belongs;
7. Classification by account, fund and jurisdiction;
8. Receipt item;
9. Other necessary matters.

Article 5 (Collection Determinations after Acceptance of Receipts)
(1) Where receipts are paid without a payment notice to a cashier, the Bank of Korea, etc., an agency under Article 92(1) (hereinafter referred to as a “treasury agency”), a postal agency established by the Minister of Science and ICT (hereinafter referred to as a “postal agency”), a national tax payment agency under the portion of Article 12(1)3 of the National Tax Collection Act preceding its items, or a payment agency for national funds other than national taxes (hereinafter referred to as a “national funds payment agency”), the revenue collection officer shall make a collection determination on the basis of documentary evidence of acceptance (hereinafter referred to as “acceptance evidence”) forwarded by the relevant cashier, the Bank of Korea, etc., treasury agency, postal agency or national funds payment agency. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2013.3.23, 2021.3.16, 2023.1.17>
(2) The date of a collection determination under paragraph (1) shall be the date acceptance evidence is received; where it is received after the month of acceptance, the year, month and day of acceptance shall be indicated: Provided, That where acceptance evidence is received after the fiscal year of acceptance, collection shall be determined as receipts of the fiscal year in which acceptance occurred. <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 6 (Collection Determinations for Installment Amounts) Where receipts are to be paid in installments under statutes, etc. or for other reasons, the revenue collection officer shall divide the receipts according to the number of installments and make fresh collection determinations.

Article 7 (Collection Determinations for Returned Amounts) Where returned amounts are included in receipts under Article 29(2) of the Act, the revenue collection officer shall make a collection determination by applying Article 5 mutatis mutandis.

Article 8 (Collection Determinations for Substitute Payments) Where receipts for which collection has been determined are paid with revenue stamps or postage stamps, or in kind, under other statutes or regulations, the revenue collection officer shall account for the corresponding amount as accepted receipts and make a collection determination reducing the amount by the substitute payment.

Article 9 (Changes to Collection Determinations)
(1) Where a revenue collection officer intends to change an amount, item, etc. already determined for collection because of an amendment to statutes, etc., a calculation error or another reason, the officer shall clearly state the basis and change the determination using the Item Correction Resolution in attached Form 3 and the Error Correction (Reduction) Resolution in attached Form 4.
(2) In changing a collection determination under paragraph (1), where entries in a Payment Notice in attached Form 5 are changed after its issuance, the revenue collection officer shall print and retain the Receipts Collection Resolution stating the reason for the change, and notify the payer of the changes by forwarding the Payment Form in attached Form 6.

SECTION 2 PAYMENT NOTICES

Article 10 (Written Payment Notices)
(1) Upon making a collection determination, the revenue collection officer shall issue a Payment Notice in attached Form 5 stating the matters in the subparagraphs of Article 4 under the main clause of Article 9 of the Decree, and deliver or send it to the payer by mail, etc.: Provided, That a payment notice need not be issued where payment is required under Articles 11 and 12.
(2) Where a payment notice is returned because the payer's address is unknown or for another reason, the revenue collection officer shall verify the payer's name, address, etc. and serve it by registered mail; where the payer is absent from the place of service and the notice sent by registered mail is returned, service shall be made by public notice.

Article 10-2 (Performance of Printing and Dispatch of Notices on Behalf of Revenue Collection Officers)
(1) When giving notice under Article 10 of the Act, a revenue collection officer may have an institution designated by the Minister of Finance and Economy (hereinafter referred to as a “notice agency”) print and dispatch notices on the officer's behalf. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Upon printing and dispatching notices under paragraph (1), a notice agency shall immediately notify the revenue collection officer of the result.
[Newly inserted 2007.11.6]

Article 11 (Oral Payment Notices) Where giving an oral payment notice under the proviso to Article 9 of the Decree, the revenue collection officer shall notify the relevant revenue cashier and cashier for funds for advance use of the amount payable and other matters necessary for payment.

Article 12 (Payment Notices by Public Announcement) Where giving payment notice by public announcement under statutes or regulations, the revenue collection officer shall clearly state the notice matters under the subparagraphs of Article 4.

Article 13 (Payment Notices by Electronic Service)
(1) Where an electronic service agency under Article 10(1) of the Decree electronically serves a payment notice under Article 11 of the Act and makes two or more dispatch attempts within three days from issuance, but service fails because the payer's email address is closed or for another reason, the agency shall immediately notify the revenue collection officer.
(2) In cases under paragraph (1), the revenue collection officer shall give the payment notice by the method prescribed in Article 10. The officer shall notify the payer in advance that future payment notices will also be dispatched under Article 10.

Article 14 (Payment Notices by Payment Forms)
(1) A revenue collection officer shall send a Payment Form in attached Form 6 to the payer in the following cases:
1. The payer applies to pay in installments within the deadline in an already dispatched payment notice;
2. The payer requests redispatch of a payment notice;
3. The competent revenue collection officer for unaccepted receipts changes after dispatch of the payment notice;
4. Entries in a payment notice or payment form differ from the collection determination and are to be changed;
5. Following dispatch of a payment notice, the item is changed or the amount determined for collection is reduced before payment;
6. Following dispatch of a payment notice, a setoff occurs and an amount remains to be accepted.
(2) Where a payer pays without a payment notice as prescribed by statutes, etc., the payer shall indicate “Payment before collection determination” at the top of the Payment Form in attached Form 6 and make payment.
(3) When sending a payment form under paragraph (1), the revenue collection officer shall specify the reason and details of issuance in its description field.
(4) When electronically serving a payment notice under Article 10(3) of the Decree, the revenue collection officer shall have the electronic service agency electronically serve the payment form under paragraph (1) on the payer.

Article 15 (Payer's Name) When dispatching a payment notice or payment form, the revenue collection officer shall state the corporation's name for a corporate payer and the relevant institution's name for a government office.

Article 16 (Place of Payment)
(1) When dispatching a payment notice or payment form, the revenue collection officer shall designate a revenue cashier, cashier for funds for advance use, the Bank of Korea, etc., treasury agency, postal agency or national funds payment agency as the place of payment: Provided, That where giving notice under Article 12, the place of payment shall be a revenue cashier or cashier for funds for advance use. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(2) When dispatching a payment notice or payment form requiring the payer to pay receipts to a revenue cashier or cashier for funds for advance use, the revenue collection officer shall notify the relevant cashier.
(3) When designating the Bank of Korea, etc., a treasury agency, postal agency or national funds payment agency as the place of payment, the revenue collection officer may not designate a particular financial company, etc. or its business office: Provided, That this does not apply where amounts recovered from national funds invested under Article 34(1) and (3) of the Act are required to be paid to the Bank of Korea. <Amended 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4>

Article 17 (Payment Notice Numbers)
(1) Each payment notice shall bear a unique number for each payer according to the following classification:
1. Where statutes or regulations fix a payment period: A serial number assigned for each payment period;
2. In cases other than subparagraph 1: A serial number assigned throughout the fiscal year.
(2) Where assigning a payment notice number under paragraph (1) is difficult, a revenue collection officer may assign a separate number.
(3) Paragraphs (1) and (2) apply mutatis mutandis to issuance of payment forms under Article 14.

SECTION 3 ELECTRONIC SERVICE AGENCIES, ETC.

Article 18 (Applications for Designation as Electronic Service Agencies) A person wishing to be designated as an electronic service agency under Article 10(1) of the Decree shall apply to the Minister of Finance and Economy, attaching the following documents to the application for designation: <Amended 2007.11.6, 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
1. Copy of business registration certificate;
2. Documents evidencing development and installation of a system capable of connecting with the digital budget and accounting system under Article 10(3) of the Decree;
3. Other documents considered necessary by the Minister of Finance and Economy.

Article 19 (Revocation of Designation as an Electronic Service Agency)
(1) “Reasons prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 10(2) of the Decree means cases in which an electronic service agency becomes unable to continue performing electronic service because of a prolonged outage, etc. of the information and communications media and programs necessary for performing the service on behalf of another. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) When intending to revoke designation of an electronic service agency under Article 10(2) of the Decree, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall hold a hearing for that agency. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) When revoking designation of an electronic service agency, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall notify the heads of central government agencies and publicly announce the fact. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(4) Upon receiving notification under paragraph (3), the head of a central government agency shall have subordinate revenue collection officers individually notify applicants for electronic service that designation of the relevant agency has been revoked. <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 20 (Applications for Electronic Service) “Other matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 10(4)4 of the Decree means means of contacting the applicant, such as the applicant's telephone number. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 21 (Payment of Costs for Electronic Service) Under Article 10(7) of the Decree, the head of a central government agency shall determine an amount per service within the budget, considering service performance and costs of electronic service, and pay once a year the amount calculated on that basis according to the number of notices served.

Article 22 (Provision of Payment Notice Information) “Other matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 12, subparagraph 7, of the Decree means classification by fiscal year, account, fund and jurisdiction. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

SECTION 4 ACCEPTANCE OF RECEIPTS

Article 23 (Notification of Acceptance of Receipts) Upon accepting receipts under Article 14(1) of the Decree, a revenue cashier shall notify the revenue collection officer of the details of acceptance, attaching a copy of the Payment Receipt Certificate in attached Form 6.

Article 24 (Payment of Receipts to the Bank of Korea, etc.) A revenue cashier shall pay cash, etc. received to the Bank of Korea, etc., treasury agencies or postal agencies without delay using the Payment Form in attached Form 6, and obtain a receipt certificate: Provided, That cash, etc. received after those institutions close for business shall be paid immediately the following day. <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 25 (Acceptance of Receipts Abroad)
(1) Articles 23 and 24 apply mutatis mutandis to acceptance of receipts abroad: Provided, That receipts accepted in foreign currency shall be paid to the Bank of Korea, etc. in foreign currency.
(2) In cases under paragraph (1), the receipt delivered to the payer and the receipt certificate retained by the receiving institution shall state the amount accepted in won; where accepted in foreign currency, the foreign currency amount and exchange rate at the time shall also be stated.

Article 26 (Payment into the Treasury of Receipts Accepted Abroad)
(1) Where receipts are accepted abroad and no business office of the Bank of Korea, etc. exists in that locality, the revenue cashier shall remit and pay them into the Bank of Korea, etc. in Korea.
(2) Where receipts accepted abroad cannot be paid in immediately, the revenue cashier may convert each month's receipts into a bill of exchange and pay it into the Bank of Korea, etc. with a payment form on the first day of the following month. The payment form shall state the amount in won and also the face value of the bill.

Article 27 (Submission of Statements of Receipts Paid In) A revenue cashier shall prepare a monthly statement of receipts paid in on the basis of the cash transactions ledger under Article 92(4) of the Decree, and submit it to the revenue collection officer by the third of the following month.

Article 28 (Acceptance Procedures of National Funds Receiving Institutions)
(1) Upon accepting receipts from a payer or revenue cashier, the Bank of Korea, etc., treasury agencies, postal agencies and national funds payment agencies shall transmit acceptance details to the Bank of Korea without delay: Provided, That upon accepting receipts under Article 14(2), a copy of the Payment Receipt Certificate in attached Form 6 shall be sent to the revenue collection officer. <Amended 2015.11.26>
(2) The Bank of Korea receiving acceptance details under paragraph (1) shall account for them as receipts of the fiscal year to which the acceptance date belongs: Provided, That in any of the following cases, the Bank shall account for them as receipts of the fiscal year immediately preceding the fiscal year of acceptance: <Amended 2015.11.26>
1. Receipts are accepted by January 20 of the following fiscal year under the proviso to Article 5(2) of the Decree;
2. The revenue collection officer requests a change of the fiscal year of receipts under Article 28-2.
(3) Upon completing accounting under paragraph (2), the Bank of Korea shall notify the revenue collection officer of the acceptance details through the digital budget and accounting system.
(4) Postal agencies and national funds payment agencies shall deposit cash accepted under paragraph (1) in State deposits at the Bank of Korea by the deadline designated by the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2026.1.2>
[Wholly amended 2008.10.1]

Article 28-2 (Requests to Change the Fiscal Year of Accepted Receipts)
(1) Where receipts have their payment deadline extended for a reason falling under Article 13(3) of the Decree, Article 5(1) of the Framework Act on National Taxes, Article 8(3) of the Customs Act, etc. and are accepted on the first business day of the following fiscal year after the fiscal year containing the unextended deadline, the revenue collection officer shall request the Bank of Korea by January 20 to account for those receipts as receipts of the fiscal year immediately preceding the fiscal year of acceptance.
(2) Articles 128 through 130 apply mutatis mutandis to correction of errors by the Bank of Korea pursuant to a fiscal-year change request under paragraph (1), correction of errors after the end of a fiscal year and adjustment of accounting books.
[Newly inserted 2015.11.26]

SECTION 5 RETURN OF ERRONEOUS PAYMENTS AND OVERPAYMENTS, ETC.

Article 29 (Determinations to Return Erroneous Payments and Overpayments)
(1) Where receipts are paid in excess of the amount that should have been accepted because of errors, duplication, etc. in collection determination or acceptance, the revenue collection officer shall determine return of the erroneous or excess amount using the Erroneous Payment and Overpayment Return Resolution in attached Form 6-2. <Amended 2003.12.31>
(2) A determination of return under paragraph (1) is deemed a reduction in the amount determined for collection for the fiscal year in which the return determination is made.

Article 30 (Notification of Determinations to Return Erroneous Payments and Overpayments)
(1) When notifying a person who made an erroneous payment or overpayment of a return determination, or notifying a receipt refund determination, under Article 17(1) and (4) of the Decree, the revenue collection officer shall use the Notice of Determination to Return Erroneous Payments and Overpayments in attached Form 7 or the Notice of Determination to Refund Receipts in attached Form 8.
(2) Article 10(2) applies mutatis mutandis where a notice under paragraph (1) is returned.

Article 31 (Refund of Receipts) Articles 29 and 30 apply mutatis mutandis to refunds of receipts under Article 17(4) of the Decree. In such cases, receipt refund determinations shall use attached Form 8-2. <Amended 2003.12.31>

Article 31-2 (Procedures for Payment of Local Consumption Tax Collected by the State)
(1) “Collection details prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 18-2(2) of the Decree means the following details: <Amended 2026.1.2>
1. Receipt year;
2. Amount collected;
3. Amount refunded;
4. Amount transferred to the local consumption tax account;
5. Amount to be received by transfer from the local consumption tax account.
(2) “Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 18-2(6) of the Decree means the following: <Amended 2026.1.2>
1. Matters to be stated when requesting a transfer from the Bank of Korea:
(a) Year, month and day of transfer;
(b) Account or subaccount from which withdrawal is made;
(c) Amount transferred;
(d) Account or subaccount into which transfer is made;
2. Matters to be stated when requesting payment from the Bank of Korea:
(a) Year, month and day of payment;
(b) Account or subaccount;
(c) Amount paid;
(d) Real-name identification number of the payment administrator;
(e) Deposit bank and account number of the payment administrator.
[Newly inserted 2010.1.8]

SECTION 6 MANAGEMENT OF RECEIPTS, ETC.

Article 32 (Demands for Payment, etc.)
(1) Where a payer fails to pay receipts by the deadline, the revenue collection officer shall dispatch a Demand for Payment in attached Form 10 within seven days after the deadline; if payment is not made within the deadline specified in that demand, the officer may dispatch one additional demand. <Amended 2003.12.31>
(2) The payment deadline for a demand dispatched under paragraph (1) shall be within ten days from dispatch.
(3) Where payment is not made by the deadline despite service by public notice under Article 10(2), the revenue collection officer shall notify the institution responsible for the relevant claim.

Article 33 Deleted. <2003.12.31>

Article 34 (Carryover of Amounts Determined for Collection)
(1) The revenue collection officer shall carry over unaccepted amounts among each fiscal year's amounts determined for collection as amounts determined for collection of receipts of the following fiscal year.
(2) Amounts carried over under paragraph (1) shall be entered as at January 1 of the following fiscal year in the relevant items of the receipts collection ledger under Article 92(1) of the Decree, separately from that fiscal year's amounts and indicating carryover from the preceding fiscal year: Provided, That amounts carried over because of national funds transfers between government subaccounts shall be separately entered as at January 21 of the following fiscal year, indicating carryover from the preceding fiscal year. <Amended 2015.11.26>
(3) Where an amount determined for collection and carried over from a preceding fiscal year remains unaccepted, it shall be carried over again in accordance with paragraph (2).

Article 35 (Determinations to Write Off Uncollectible Amounts)
(1) Upon receiving notification of a debt waiver under other statutes or regulations, or where an amount determined for collection can no longer be accepted because of completion of prescription or another reason, the revenue collection officer shall prepare documents stating the reason and determine a write-off as uncollectible.
(2) Upon making a write-off determination under paragraph (1), the revenue collection officer shall separately indicate it in the Receipts Collection Resolution in attached Form 1.

Article 36 (Reports of Objections, etc.) Where an objection, administrative adjudication appeal or lawsuit is filed concerning a collection determination, the revenue collection officer shall report the fact to the head of the central government agency.

CHAPTER III FUNDS FOR ADVANCE USE

Article 37 (Deposit and Management of Funds for Advance Use) The head of an institution operating funds for advance use that handles deposit business may not appoint a public official responsible for deposit receipts and payments as cashier for funds for advance use: Provided, That an exception applies where an unduly small staff complement or another unavoidable reason requires such appointment; in such cases, the officer authorizing transactions in funds for advance use shall keep and manage the treasury deposit passbook and registered seal.

Article 38 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) Articles 23, 27, 54, 55, 64 and 66 through 70 apply mutatis mutandis to cashiers for funds for advance use.

CHAPTER IV DISBURSEMENTS

SECTION 1 COMMITMENTS TO DISBURSE, ETC.

Article 39 (Preparation of Commitment-to-Disburse Documents, etc.) When making a commitment to disburse, a finance officer shall prepare a Commitment-to-Disburse Document in attached Form 11 and attached Form 11-2 and enter it in the Commitment-to-Disburse Ledger in attached Form 12. <Amended 2007.11.6>
[Wholly amended 2003.12.31]

Article 40 (Commitments to Disburse under Construction Contracts, etc.) For construction, manufacturing or service contracts, the finance officer shall use the total contract amount as the amount committed to disburse, and may request the disbursing officer to pay the construction price in part according to the degree of completion, etc.

Article 41 (Notification of Changes to Commitments to Disburse) Where a finance officer changes a commitment to disburse under statutes, etc., the officer shall notify the disbursing officer of the changes. The same applies when correcting an incorrectly entered accounting item, etc.

Article 42 (Forwarding of Documents concerning Commitments to Disburse)
(1) Before the time for disbursement under relevant statutes or regulations, etc. arrives, the finance officer shall forward the commitment-to-disburse document to the disbursing officer, attaching the contract, design specifications, product specifications, inspection report and other documents concerning the commitment.
(2) When forwarding documents under paragraph (1), the finance officer shall also forward materials necessary for account transfer, such as a copy of the deposit passbook showing the account number at a bank, etc. (meaning a bank under the Banking Act or another institution performing financial business; hereinafter referred to as a “bank, etc.”) of the creditor, etc. under Article 22(3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “creditor, etc.”). <Amended 2011.10.4>

Article 43 (Legitimate Creditors, etc.)
(1) A deposit account at a bank, etc. of a creditor, etc. under Article 42(2) shall be opened in the real name of the creditor, etc. stated in the commitment documents: Provided, That where the creditor's, etc. death or another reason prevents payment into an account in the name of the party stated in the commitment documents, payment may be made into an account in the name of the successor to the claim. <Amended 2011.10.4>
(2) Where a construction, manufacturing or purchase contract constitutes a subcontract under Article 2(1) of the Fair Transactions in Subcontracting Act and the subcontract consideration is paid directly to the relevant subcontractor, that subcontractor is deemed a creditor, etc. under paragraph (1). <Amended 2005.6.30>
(3) A finance officer intending to transfer cash into an account under the proviso to paragraph (1) shall attach documents evidencing succession to the claim and forward them to the disbursing officer.

SECTION 2 DISBURSEMENT PROCEDURES

Article 44 (Preparation of Disbursement Resolutions) A disbursing officer shall disburse using a Disbursement Resolution in attached Form 13 and attached Form 13-2 and record the result in the Disbursements Ledger in attached Form 14. <Amended 2007.11.6>

Article 45 (Account Transfers)
(1) A national funds deposit request or national funds transfer deposit request under Article 28(2) of the Decree (hereinafter referred to as a “national funds deposit request, etc.”) shall state the following:
1. Fiscal year and account name;
2. Amount payable;
3. Creditor's real-name identification number;
4. Creditor's deposit account number;
5. Name of the revenue collection officer (only for national funds transfer deposits);
6. Year, month and day of issuance of the request, etc. and issuer.
(2) When requesting account transfer from the Bank of Korea, etc. under Article 28(2) of the Decree, the disbursing officer shall first verify the accuracy, etc. of the account number at the bank, etc. designated by the creditor, etc. <Amended 2011.10.4>
(3) Upon being notified by the Bank of Korea, etc. of an error in an account to which transfer is intended, the disbursing officer shall check the details and resend a national funds deposit request, etc. stating the new account number.

Article 46 (Disbursement Procedures during Outages of Information and Communications Media, etc.)
(1) When printing and forwarding a national funds deposit request, etc. to the Bank of Korea, etc. under Article 29(2) of the Decree, the disbursing officer shall forward it to the head of the central government agency and have that head forward it to the Bank of Korea, etc.
(2) When forwarding a national funds deposit request, etc. to the Bank of Korea, etc. on behalf of the disbursing officer under paragraph (1), the head of the central government agency shall affix the head's seal registered with the Bank of Korea, etc. to it and send it by hand, mail or fax. <Amended 2021.10.28>
(3) Before forwarding a request, etc. to the Bank of Korea, etc. under paragraph (2), the head of the central government agency shall notify it in advance of the contents, method, etc.
(4) Where requested by the Bank of Korea, etc. because of a large volume of disbursements or another reason, the head of the central government agency may record the requests, etc. under paragraph (1) on information and communications recording media, such as diskettes or magnetic tapes, and forward them to the Bank of Korea, etc.

Article 47 (Disbursement by Treasury Checks)
(1) When issuing treasury checks under Article 30(1) of the Decree, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall issue checks payable to bearer. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Upon receiving notification of disbursement by treasury checks under Article 30(2) of the Decree, the head of a central government agency shall appoint one disbursing officer for each accounting subaccount, jurisdiction and fund (one or more where approved by the Minister of Finance and Economy), and have the officer obtain check forms from the Bank of Korea, etc. and disburse. The head shall notify the Bank of Korea, etc. of the detailed monthly cash plan by disbursing officer. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) Where payment is made by issuing treasury checks under paragraph (1), the Minister of Finance and Economy may prescribe matters necessary for payment methods and procedures, etc. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 48 (Notification of Transfer Results) Upon completing an account transfer under Articles 45 and 46, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall notify the disbursing officer of the result.

Article 49 (Disbursements Subject to Deductions) Where an amount to be disbursed includes tax to be withheld under the Income Tax Act or Corporate Tax Act, additional tax collected specially under the Local Tax Act, or another amount to be deducted, the disbursing officer shall state the deduction details in the Disbursement Resolution in attached Form 13 and disburse the balance after deduction. <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 50 (Procedures for Payment of Deductions, etc.) When disbursing under Article 49, the disbursing officer shall pay the deducted amount within the payment deadline prescribed by relevant statutes or regulations, etc.

Article 51 (Obtaining Receipt Certificates, etc.)
(1) Where paying cash, etc. under Article 22(4) of the Act, a disbursing officer shall obtain a receipt certificate. <Amended 2003.12.31>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where the creditor, etc. is a business entity under the Value-Added Tax Act, a tax invoice under Article 32 of that Act, an invoice under Article 163 of the Income Tax Act, or an invoice under Article 121 of the Corporate Tax Act shall be obtained. <Amended 2005.6.30, 2013.6.28>

SECTION 3 SPECIAL CASES FOR DISBURSEMENT

Article 52 (Scope of Office Operating Expenses)
(1) The maximum expense payable as an office operating expense under Article 31, subparagraph 1, of the Decree shall be 5,000,000 won per transaction: Provided, That this does not apply to any of the following: <Amended 2007.11.6, 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2023.1.17, 2026.1.2>
1. Expenses directly required for the relevant business under an enterprise special account;
2. Public charges and committee attendance expenses among operating expenses;
3. Expenses for investigative activities among special activity expenses;
4. Expenses for intelligence activities among national security expenses;
5. Expenses for intelligence activities among information security expenses;
6. Other expenses determined by the Minister of Finance and Economy.
(2) Expenses payable as office operating expenses under Article 31, subparagraph 4, of the Decree are as follows: <Amended 2007.11.6, 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2026.1.2>
1. Salaries of active-duty enlisted soldiers and special-area service allowances among personnel expenses;
2. Deleted. <2007.11.6>
3. Among compensatory payments: military death compensation, lump-sum death payments for persons of national merit or their survivors, soldiers' discharge benefits, reserve forces travel expenses, travel expenses for operation of full-time reserve service and public service systems, return travel expenses for persons failing military induction physical examinations, hospitality expenses for military bereaved families, rewards, prizes, and reimbursement of actual costs such as daily allowances to witnesses, expert witnesses, interpreters or translators under statutes or regulations;
4. Deleted. <2007.11.6>
5. Relief and correctional expenses among transfers to the private sector;
6. Other expenses the Minister of Finance and Economy considers suitable for payment as office operating expenses because of their nature.

Article 53 (Delivery of Office Operating Expenses) When delivering additional office operating expenses under Article 32(2) of the Decree, the disbursing officer shall minimize the balance of treasury deposits held by the office operating expense cashier, considering payment timing, treasury deposit balances, etc.

Article 54 (Opening Treasury Deposit Accounts)
(1) An office operating expense cashier intending to open a treasury deposit account under Article 32(5) of the Decree shall submit the following documents to the financial company, etc.: <Amended 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4, 2013.6.28>
1. Application for treasury deposit transactions (as prescribed by the financial company, etc.);
2. Copy of the document assigning a unique identification number under Article 12(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act;
3. Other documents prescribed by the Bank of Korea, etc. or the financial company, etc.
(2) When opening a treasury deposit account under paragraph (1), the registered seal and password shall be registered and a passbook obtained. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(3) The seal under paragraph (2) shall be the official seal of the office operating expense cashier: Provided, That where necessary, the head of the agency may require the cashier's personal seal to be affixed additionally. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(4) The password under paragraph (2) shall be changed whenever the office operating expense cashier is replaced. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(5) For separate accounting of treasury deposits, financial companies, etc. shall establish treasury deposit subaccounts and notify the Bank of Korea, etc. of treasury deposit transactions through an information and communications system. <Amended 2011.10.4>
(6) The Governor of the Bank of Korea shall prescribe details concerning opening and operation of treasury deposit accounts other than those in paragraphs (1) through (5). <Amended 2008.10.1>
(7) Upon prescribing matters concerning opening and operation of treasury deposits under paragraph (6), the Governor of the Bank of Korea shall notify the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 55 (Prohibition against Multiple Treasury Deposit Accounts)
(1) An office operating expense cashier may not open two or more treasury deposit accounts simultaneously: Provided, That this does not apply in the following cases: <Amended 2011.10.4>
1. Opening a new treasury deposit account before closing the previous account in order to change accounts;
2. Depositing office operating expenses by currency with banks, etc. or foreign banks, etc. at an overseas diplomatic mission under Article 39 of the Decree.
(2) An office operating expense cashier opening, changing or closing a treasury deposit account under paragraph (1) and Article 54 shall notify the disbursing officer, the head of the central government agency and the Bank of Korea, etc.

Article 56 (Standards for Payment) Upon receiving a payment request from a creditor, etc., an office operating expense cashier shall examine the legitimacy of the request before making payment.

Article 57 (Preparation of Payment Resolutions, etc.)
(1) Where an office operating expense cashier uses government purchase cards under Article 24(5) of the Act, the cashier may prepare a single payment resolution for each budget item when paying the charges for use of those cards.
(2) An office operating expense cashier shall pay using the Payment Resolution in attached Form 14-2 and record the result in the Cash Transactions Ledger in attached Form 31.
[Wholly amended 2003.12.31]

Article 58 (Handling Government Purchase Card Affairs, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall require persons falling under any subparagraph of Article 35 of the Decree who intend to issue and operate government purchase cards under that Article (hereinafter referred to as “cards”) (hereinafter referred to as “credit card business operators, etc.”) to maintain facilities enabling the State and the relevant operator, etc. to provide one another with information on spending limits by budget item, usage details, etc. through an information and communications system. <Amended 2017.12.29, 2026.1.2>
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall notify heads of central government agencies of credit card business operators, etc. with the facilities under paragraph (1), and those heads shall notify subordinate cashiers. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2026.1.2>

Article 59 (Conclusion of Card Use Agreements)
(1) When intending to conclude a card use agreement with a credit card business operator, etc. under Article 35 of the Decree, an office operating expense cashier shall select an operator, etc. notified by the Minister of Finance and Economy under Article 58(2). <Amended 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2026.1.2>
(2) Upon concluding an agreement under paragraph (1) (including an agreement concluded upon changing the credit card business operator, etc.), an office operating expense cashier shall report to the head of the central government agency to which the cashier belongs. <Amended 2017.12.29>
(3) The Minister of Finance and Economy may separately prescribe guidelines for agreements, etc. concluded between office operating expense cashiers and credit card business operators, etc. under paragraph (1). <Amended 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2026.1.2>

Article 60 (Issuance and Management of Cards)
(1) An office operating expense cashier shall apply to a credit card business operator, etc. for issuance of cards by budget item and card user. <Amended 2017.12.29, 2019.7.1>
(2) When applying under paragraph (1), a password shall be assigned to each card. <Amended 2019.7.1>
(3) An office operating expense cashier shall prepare and maintain a card issuance register, and keep card numbers and passwords secure. <Amended 2019.7.1>
(4) A card user shall keep and manage issued cards with the same care as cash. <Amended 2019.7.1>
(5) Where a card user loses authority to use a card because of a departmental transfer or another reason, the office operating expense cashier shall recover the card without delay [for electronic debit payment means under Article 2, subparagraph 13, of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act (excluding debit cards under Article 2, subparagraph 6, of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act; hereinafter referred to as “electronic debit payment means”), meaning revocation of that user's use authority]. <Newly inserted 2019.7.1>

Article 61 (Changes of Credit Card Business Operators, etc.)
(1) An office operating expense cashier intending to change the credit card business operator, etc. with which a card use agreement has been concluded shall conclude an agreement with a new operator, etc. under Article 59, obtain new cards, and then terminate the previous agreement. <Amended 2017.12.29, 2019.7.1>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where an office operating expense cashier concludes an agreement for use of electronic debit payment means with a new credit card business operator, etc., the cashier need not terminate the agreement with the previous operator, etc.: Provided, That if any electronic debit payment means cease to be used because of the new agreement, the agreement for use of those means shall be terminated. <Newly inserted 2019.7.1>
[Title amended 2017.12.29]

Article 62 (Use of Cards)
(1) Upon receiving office operating expenses from a disbursing officer, an office operating expense cashier shall immediately notify the credit card business operator, etc. of spending limits by budget item through the digital budget and accounting system. <Amended 2007.11.6, 2017.12.29>
(2) A public official using a card issued to an office operating expense cashier (hereinafter referred to as a “card user”) may not exceed the spending limits by budget item under paragraph (1).

Article 63 (Reporting Lost Cards) Upon losing a card, the card user shall immediately report the loss to the credit card business operator, etc. and notify the office operating expense cashier. <Amended 2017.12.29>

Article 64 (Payment of Office Operating Expenses by Account Transfer, etc.) When making an account transfer or withdrawing treasury deposits for payment under Article 36 of the Decree, an office operating expense cashier shall comply with the treasury deposit terms and conditions and rules of the financial company, etc. with which transactions are conducted. <Amended 2011.10.4>
[Wholly amended 2003.12.31]

Article 65 (Cash Payments) Cash payments under Article 36(1)1 of the Decree may be made for the following purposes: <Amended 2007.11.6, 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2023.1.17, 2026.1.2>
1. Salaries of active-duty enlisted soldiers and special-area service allowances among personnel expenses;
2. Deleted. <2007.11.6>
3. Various fees, usage charges, operating allowances and division operating expenses among operating expenses;
4. Fixed overseas business trip expenses among business promotion expenses;
5. Among compensatory payments: military death compensation, lump-sum death payments for persons of national merit or their survivors, soldiers' discharge benefits, reserve forces travel expenses, travel expenses for operation of full-time reserve service and public service systems, return travel expenses for persons failing military induction physical examinations, hospitality expenses for military bereaved families, rewards, prizes, and reimbursement of actual costs such as daily allowances to witnesses, expert witnesses, interpreters or translators under statutes or regulations;
6. Deleted. <2007.11.6>
7. Relief and correctional expenses among transfers to the private sector;
8. Expenses such as goodwill and consolation payments for which payment by account transfer or card is difficult and cash payment is unavoidable;
9. Expenses directly required for specific duties such as investigative or intelligence activities among special activity expenses, for which cash payment is unavoidable;
10. Expenses directly required for intelligence activities among national security expenses, for which cash payment is unavoidable;
11. Expenses directly required for intelligence activities among information security expenses, for which cash payment is unavoidable;
12. Other expenses the Minister of Finance and Economy considers to require unavoidable cash use because of their purpose.

Article 66 (Deductions from Office Operating Expenses) Articles 49 and 50 apply mutatis mutandis where an office operating expense cashier must deduct in advance, from an amount payable to a creditor, etc., tax to be withheld under the Income Tax Act or Corporate Tax Act, special additional tax under the Local Tax Act, etc. <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 67 (Payment of Office Operating Expenses by Transfer)
(1) Where paying treasury deposits into the National Treasury because of setoff, tax withholding, etc. of national funds, an office operating expense cashier shall present the passbook and a withdrawal slip bearing the registered seal to the financial company, etc. under Article 64 and pay the relevant revenue collection officer. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4>
(2) Paragraph (1) applies mutatis mutandis to payments to local governments. <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 68 (Obtaining Receipt Certificates, etc.) When paying office operating expenses in cash, an office operating expense cashier shall obtain a receipt certificate, etc. from the creditor, etc. or prepare a statement of reasons, as prescribed by Rules of the Board of Audit and Inspection. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>
[Title amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4]

Article 69 (Return of Payments)
(1) An office operating expense cashier may have paid amounts returned to the relevant treasury deposit account.
(2) When intending to have an amount paid returned to the treasury deposit account under paragraph (1), the office operating expense cashier shall adopt a return resolution using the Return Resolution in attached Form 14-3, and send a National Funds Return Notice in attached Form 15 to the person obliged to return it. <Amended 2003.12.31>
(3) Where an amount for which a return notice was issued in the relevant fiscal year under paragraph (2) is accepted after January 20 of the following fiscal year, the office operating expense cashier shall return it to the revenue collection officer and report its details. <Amended 2015.11.26>
(4) Upon a report that a national funds return notice has been lost, damaged, etc., the office operating expense cashier shall prepare and send a Return Payment Form in attached Form 16 to the person obliged to return the amount.

Article 70 (Errors in Account Transfers) Article 75 applies mutatis mutandis where cash transferred by an office operating expense cashier under Article 64 is confirmed to have been transferred into an account other than that of the creditor, etc.

Article 71 (Requests for Payment from Returned Office Operating Expenses) Upon receiving a payment request from a credit card business operator, etc. concerning an amount returned under Article 37 of the Decree, the office operating expense cashier shall examine the existence of the debt, whether payment has been made, whether prescription is complete, etc. and determine whether payment is to be made. <Amended 2017.12.29>

Article 72 (Payments on an Estimated Basis) “Expenses prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy” in Article 41, subparagraph 5, of the Decree means the following expenses: <Amended 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
1. Expenses required where State affairs or projects are entrusted to or performed by another on the State's behalf;
2. Progress payments or payments for deliveries already made where a change in the contract amount is expected because of price fluctuations, design changes or other changes in contract terms under Articles 64 through 66 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party.
[Wholly amended 2003.12.31]

Article 73 (Handling Entrusted Expenses)
(1) Where entrusted by the head of a central government agency with payment of expenses under Article 43 of the Decree, the Bank of Korea, etc. or banks, etc. shall receive and pay the entrusted expenses in accordance with the purpose of entrustment. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>
(2) The Bank of Korea, etc. or banks, etc. shall establish subaccounts for each cash fund for entrusted expenses under paragraph (1), and account for them separately from other national funds. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>
(3) Where a balance of entrusted expenses remains at the end of each fiscal year, the Bank of Korea, etc. or banks, etc. shall return it to the head of the relevant central government agency by January 20 of the following fiscal year. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4, 2015.11.26>
(4) The Bank of Korea, etc. or banks, etc. shall maintain books concerning transactions in entrusted expenses and record and retain the transaction details. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>
(5) Details necessary for handling entrusted expenses shall be determined by the head of the central government agency in consultation with the Governor of the Bank of Korea, etc. or the head of the relevant bank, etc. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>
[Title amended 2003.12.31]

SECTION 4 RETURN OF DISBURSED FUNDS

Article 74 (Return of Disbursed Funds)
(1) Where a disbursing officer intends to have a disbursed amount returned to the budget item from which it was disbursed under Article 45 of the Decree, the officer shall send a National Funds Return Notice in attached Form 15 to the person obliged to return it.
(2) Upon receiving notice from the Bank of Korea, etc. of acceptance of a returned amount under Article 46 of the Decree and Article 106 of these Rules, the disbursing officer shall report the fact to the head of the central government agency.

Article 75 (Return of Disbursed Funds following Errors in Account Transfers) Where funds disbursed by account transfer under Articles 28 and 29 of the Decree have been transferred into an account other than that of the creditor, etc., or an amount exceeding the amount to be disbursed has been paid, the disbursing officer shall immediately take the return procedures under Article 74.

Article 76 (Issuance of Return Payment Forms) Where a person obliged to return disbursed funds requests reissuance of a national funds return notice, the disbursing officer shall send a Return Payment Form in attached Form 16.

CHAPTER V SETOFF

Article 77 (Setoff)
(1) Where the State's debt and claim relate to the same person, revenue collection officers, disbursing officers and cashiers may set them off under the Civil Act. <Amended 2005.6.30>
(2) Upon making a setoff under paragraph (1), the result shall be notified to the public officials engaged in accounting responsible for the receipts and disbursed funds subject to setoff, using the Setoff Amount Statement in attached Form 17.

Article 78 (Setoff by Revenue Collection Officers)
(1) Upon making a collection determination for receipts subject to setoff under Article 77, the revenue collection officer shall, for the amount corresponding to the setoff, additionally state the official post and name of the disbursing officer or cashier on the payment notice and send it to that officer or cashier, marking “Setoff amount” in the margin on the face of the notice. The same applies upon request by a disbursing officer or cashier.
(2) When determining collection of receipts subject to setoff, the revenue collection officer shall include the setoff amount in the determination.

Article 79 (Setoff by Disbursing Officers)
(1) When making a setoff under Article 77, the disbursing officer shall pay the setoff amount to the revenue collection officer by transfer and notify that officer of the result.
(2) Where an amount remains to be accepted by the State after setoff under paragraph (1), the disbursing officer shall notify the revenue collection officer, clearly stating the setoff amount, additional amount to be accepted, counterparty to the setoff, etc.; where an amount remains payable by the State, the balance shall be paid.

Article 80 (Setoff by Cashiers)
(1) When making a setoff under Article 77, an office operating expense cashier shall pay into the revenue collection officer's account, attaching the payment notice and setoff amount statement for the setoff amount.
(2) In cases under paragraph (1), where the creditor, etc. has set off a debt owed to an agency other than that to which the office operating expense cashier belongs, the cashier shall obtain a payment notice from the revenue collection officer of that other agency and take payment procedures.
(3) Article 79(2) applies mutatis mutandis where a surplus or shortfall remains after setoff under paragraph (1).

CHAPTER VI ISSUANCE OF TREASURY BILLS AND TRANSFER OF NATIONAL FUNDS <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 81 (Issuance by Subscription)
(1) A person wishing to subscribe where treasury bills are issued by subscription shall submit a subscription application together with the price at the designated place.
(2) Where the total subscribed amount exceeds the issue amount in cases under paragraph (1), allocation may be proportional to subscribed amounts. <Amended 2021.10.28>

Article 82 (Issuance by Sale) Where treasury bills are issued by sale, they may be sold at a discount calculated for the number of days from sale to maturity, or sold at face value.

Article 83 (Issuance by Competitive Bidding)
(1) Where treasury bills are issued by competitive bidding, bidders shall bid a subscribed amount and a unit subscription price (meaning a price per unit calculated using a discount rate); among bidders bidding at or below the discount rate provisionally fixed by the Minister of Finance and Economy (hereinafter referred to as the “provisional discount rate”), successful bidders shall be determined in order from the lowest discount rate until the issue amount is reached (excluding amounts allocated to bidders bidding only a subscribed amount under paragraph (4); hereinafter the same applies in this paragraph): Provided, That where the last-ranked successful bidder's subscribed amount, added to those of preceding successful bidders, exceeds the issue amount, the excess is deemed unsuccessful. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Where there are two or more last-ranked successful bidders in cases under paragraph (1), allocation shall be proportional to their subscribed amounts. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2021.10.28>
(3) Where necessary to protect ordinary investors, the Minister of Finance and Economy may allow bidders to bid only a subscribed amount on condition of allocation at the weighted arithmetic average discount rate of successful subscribed amounts under paragraphs (1) and (2). <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(4) Where allowing bids of subscribed amounts only under paragraph (3), the Minister of Finance and Economy shall determine and publicly announce the portion of the issue amount to be allocated to those bidders and other necessary matters. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 84 (Keeping the Provisional Discount Rate Available) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall keep a document stating the provisional discount rate at the place of bid opening. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 85 (Eligibility to Participate in Bidding) Where necessary, the Minister of Finance and Economy may restrict eligibility of participants in bidding. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 86 (Bidding Method) A person wishing to participate in bidding shall submit a bid in the form prescribed by the Minister of Finance and Economy to the designated place by the bidding deadline. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 87 (Bid Deposits)
(1) Where necessary, the Minister of Finance and Economy may require participants in bidding to pay a bid deposit. The Minister shall determine and publicly announce the bid deposit. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Bid deposits shall bear no interest.
(3) Bid deposits may be applied toward part of the price of treasury bills.

Article 88 (Forfeiture of Bid Deposits to the National Treasury) Where a successful bidder fails to pay the price by the designated date after receiving notice of the successful bid, that successful bid shall be invalidated. Where bid deposits were required under Article 87, the bid deposit paid by the relevant bidder shall be forfeited to the National Treasury.

Article 89 (Invalid Bids) A bid shall be invalidated in any of the following cases:
1. A person ineligible to participate takes part in bidding;
2. A bid deposit was required under Article 87 but has not been paid;
3. Matters entered in the bid are unclear;
4. The bid lacks a name and seal;
5. Another material and manifest defect exists.

Article 90 (Cash Transfers) Where the Minister of Finance and Economy intends to transfer cash between the national funds investment account under Article 76 of the Decree and respective accounts and subaccounts, or between subaccounts within the investment account, the Minister shall request the Bank of Korea to make the transfer, clearly stating the following, and notify the head of the central government agency responsible for the relevant account or subaccount: <Amended 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
1. Year, month and day of transfer;
2. Accounts or subaccounts between which cash is to be transferred and amounts.

CHAPTER VII AFFAIRS OF THE BANK OF KOREA, ETC.

SECTION 1 GENERAL RULES

Article 91 (Classification of National Funds) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall receive and disburse national funds according to the following classifications:
1. Receipts;
2. Disbursements;
3. Funds;
4. Other national funds.

Article 92 (Handling of National Funds and State Deposits)
(1) The Bank of Korea, etc. may have its principal office, branches and other offices, and the following treasury agencies handle affairs concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds and state deposits: <Amended 2005.6.30, 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4, 2016.6.30>
1. Business offices of the following financial companies, etc. designated as agencies by the Bank of Korea, etc.:
(a) Banks under Article 2, subparagraph 2 and Article 5 of the Banking Act;
(b) Financial companies, etc. under Article 11(1), subparagraphs 3 through 7 of the Decree;
2. Corporations among the following designated as agencies by their central association or federation under a contract with the Bank of Korea, etc.:
(a) Agricultural cooperatives established under the Agricultural Cooperatives Act;
(b) Fisheries cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act;
(c) Credit unions established under the Credit Unions Act;
(d) Community credit cooperatives established under the Community Credit Cooperatives Act;
(e) Mutual savings banks established under the Mutual Savings Banks Act;
(f) Forestry cooperatives established under the Forestry Cooperatives Act.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), postal authorities may handle affairs concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds and state deposits, and agencies acting on behalf of payers of national funds may handle the receipt of national funds. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(3) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. deems it necessary, it may designate a supervising office for each locality and have that office supervise affairs concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds at branches, other offices and treasury agencies (including postal authorities; hereinafter the same shall apply) within its jurisdiction.
(4) When the Bank of Korea, etc. designates or abolishes a treasury agency or supervising office under paragraphs (1) and (3), it shall notify the Minister of Finance and Economy of that fact by the end of January of the following fiscal year. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(5) Where the Minister of Finance and Economy deems a treasury agency designated under paragraph (1) unsuitable for handling affairs concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds because it violates the Act, the Decree or these Rules, or lacks an information and communications system necessary for the receipt and payment of national funds, the Minister may request the Bank of Korea, etc. to revoke the designation of that treasury agency. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(6) Where a request under paragraph (5) is made, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(7) Where the designation of a treasury agency is revoked under paragraphs (5) and (6), the designation may be revoked for all business offices of the relevant financial company, etc. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4>
(8) The Minister of Finance and Economy may restrict the handling of affairs concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds by postal authorities and agencies acting on behalf of payers of national funds under paragraph (2), in accordance with paragraph (5). <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 93 (Standards for Handling National Funds)
(1) When the principal office, branches and other offices of the Bank of Korea, etc., treasury agencies, or agencies acting on behalf of payers of national funds receive or disburse national funds, they shall, without delay, consolidate the amounts received or disbursed in the government current deposit account under Article 94 and account for them. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(2) Where the Minister of Finance and Economy deems it necessary for the efficient management of national funds, the Minister may, to the extent that the receipt and disbursement of national funds are not impeded, have the consolidation in the government current deposit account of receipts designated by the Minister among those received by treasury agencies deferred for a certain period. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) Interest determined by the Minister of Finance and Economy, taking into account the level of interest rates on ordinary deposits, may be paid on receipts whose consolidation is deferred under paragraph (2). <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 94 (Classification of Accounts for State Deposits)
(1) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall establish at its principal office a current deposit account for recording receipts and payments of national funds.
(2) Where the Minister of Finance and Economy deems it necessary to establish an account for state deposits in addition to the current deposit account under paragraph (1), the Minister may have the Bank of Korea, etc. establish such an account. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) Where a current deposit account is established under paragraph (2), all receipts and payments of deposits and transfers between deposits shall pass through the current deposit account, except as otherwise provided. <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 95 (Calculation of Interest on State Deposits) The Minister of Finance and Economy may, in consultation with the Governor of the Bank of Korea, determine details concerning the calculation and payment of interest paid by the Bank of Korea on state deposits under Article 86(3) of the Decree. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 96 (Calculation and Payment of Interest on Treasury Deposits)
(1) Interest on treasury deposits under Article 86(5) of the Decree shall not be added to the principal. On the interest calculation reference date, the Bank of Korea shall withdraw an amount equivalent to the interest calculated for each treasury deposit account and notified by the financial company, etc. from the current deposit account of that financial company, etc. opened at the Bank of Korea, and pay it as receipts of the revenue collection officer of the account, fund or subaccount to which the relevant cashier belongs. <Amended 2011.10.4>
(2) When the Bank of Korea pays an amount equivalent to interest under paragraph (1), it shall notify the relevant revenue collection officer of the details.
(3) Where notice under paragraph (2) is given, a collection determination shall be made by applying Article 5 mutatis mutandis.
(4) The interest calculation reference dates under paragraph (2) shall be April 30 and October 31 of each fiscal year, and the deadlines for payment as receipts shall be May 15 and November 15 of each fiscal year, respectively.

Article 97 (Temporary Borrowing and Repayment)
(1) Where national funds are paid in through temporary borrowing under Article 32 of the Act, the Bank of Korea shall credit them to the relevant state deposit account and notify the Minister of Finance and Economy and the public official designated by that Minister of the fact. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Where the Bank of Korea receives notice from the Minister of Finance and Economy to repay a temporary borrowing, it shall withdraw the amount from the relevant state deposit account, make the repayment, and notify the Minister and the public official designated by that Minister of the fact. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 98 (Handling of National Funds Outside Business Hours) Where the head of an agency requests the receipt or disbursement of national funds outside business hours for a special reason, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall handle the request.

Article 99 (Delegation of Affairs to the Governor of the Bank of Korea, Etc.)
(1) The Bank of Korea, etc. may determine matters concerning the handling of national funds and management of cash resources, other than matters prescribed in this Chapter, with the approval of the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall, with the approval of the Minister of Finance and Economy, determine matters necessary for supporting documents concerning the receipt and disbursement of national funds, state deposits and treasury deposits under these Rules, and for the forms, methods of recording, retention and other matters concerning the books under Article 107 and other subsidiary books. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

SECTION 2 RECEIPTS

Article 100 (Opening or Closing of Revenue Collection Officer Accounts) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. receives from the head of a central government agency a request to open or close a revenue collection officer account together with notice of the appointment or dismissal of the revenue collection officer, it shall open or close that account in the detailed receipts ledger under Article 107, subparagraph 5.

Article 101 (Return of Erroneous or Excess Payments, Etc.) Where a revenue collection officer requests payment for the return of erroneous or excess payments or for a refund of receipts under Article 17(2) and (4) of the Decree, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall transfer the amount from receipts to the payer's account at a bank, etc. In such cases, the Bank of Korea, etc. may maintain separate payment accounts for the return of erroneous or excess payments and for refunds of receipts in order to account for those returns and refunds. <Amended 2003.12.31, 2011.10.4>

Article 102 (Payment of Receipts Collected in Addition to Local Taxes) Procedures for paying in receipts collected in addition to local taxes shall be as determined by the Minister of Finance and Economy in consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2014.11.19, 2023.1.17, 2026.1.2>

SECTION 3 DISBURSEMENTS

Article 103 (Establishment of Accounts of Heads of Central Government Agencies)
(1) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. receives a request from the head of a central government agency to open or close an account, it shall open or close that head's account in the detailed cash resources planning ledger under Article 107, subparagraph 6.
(2) When requesting the opening of an account under paragraph (1), the head of the central government agency shall register a seal with the Bank of Korea, etc.

Article 104 (Recording of Monthly Detailed Cash Resources Plans) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. receives notice from the Minister of Finance and Economy of the monthly detailed cash resources plan for each central government agency, it shall record the amounts in the detailed cash resources planning ledger under Article 107, subparagraph 6 and take the necessary procedures accordingly. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>

Article 105 (Execution of Account Transfers)
(1) Where a disbursing officer requests the deposit of national funds into an account by means of a request for deposit of national funds, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall take the procedures for transferring the funds to the account of the creditor, etc.
(2) Where a disbursing officer requests a transfer entry of national funds, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall make the transfer entry into the account of the relevant revenue collection officer.

Article 106 (Procedures for Return of Disbursements)
(1) When the Bank of Korea, etc. or a treasury agency receives an amount returned by a person returning a disbursement, it shall transmit the details of the receipt to the Bank of Korea without delay.
(2) The Bank of Korea receiving the details under paragraph (1) shall treat an amount returned that belongs to the relevant fiscal year as a return of disbursements and notify the disbursing officer of the details through the digital budget and accounting system: Provided, That an amount returned after the relevant fiscal year has elapsed shall be treated as receipts of the following fiscal year, and the revenue collection officer shall be notified.
[Wholly amended 2008.10.1]

SECTION 4 BOOKS, ACCOUNTING REPORTS AND CERTIFICATION

Article 107 (Books) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall maintain the following books under Article 96 of the Decree and record daily receipts and disbursements of national funds and receipts and payments of state deposits: <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
1. General ledger of national funds;
2. Detailed ledger of receipts and payments of national funds;
3. Detailed current deposit ledger;
4. General ledger of receipts and payments of national funds;
5. Detailed receipts ledger;
6. Detailed cash resources planning ledger;
7. Detailed ledger of entrusted deposits;
8. Other detailed ledgers determined by the Minister of Finance and Economy.

Article 108 (Books for Treasury Deposits) To handle affairs under Articles 109 and 110, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall separately maintain, among the books listed in the subparagraphs of Article 107, a detailed ledger of receipts and payments of national funds, a general ledger of receipts and payments of national funds, and other necessary books, and record the daily status of receipts and payments of treasury deposits.

Article 109 (Accounting Reports on State Deposits)
(1) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall prepare a statement of financial position for national funds each day and submit it to the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2021.10.28, 2026.1.2>
(2) Where the head of the agency under whose jurisdiction a public official engaged in accounting falls or the Minister of Finance and Economy requests certification of receipts and payments of national funds or of state deposits, the Bank of Korea, etc. shall certify them and send the certification. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) The form of the statement of financial position for national funds under paragraph (1) and the method of completing it shall be as determined by the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2021.10.28, 2026.1.2>

Article 110 (Accounting Reports on Treasury Deposits)
(1) When preparing the statement of financial position for national funds under Article 109(1), the Bank of Korea, etc. shall include the status of receipts and disbursements of treasury deposits. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2021.10.28>
(2) Where the head of the agency to which a public official engaged in accounting belongs or the Minister of Finance and Economy requests certification of treasury deposits, the Bank of Korea, etc. and financial companies, etc. shall certify them and send the certification. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4, 2026.1.2>

CHAPTER VIII CASHIERS

Article 111 (Handling of Securities) Where a cashier receives securities under Article 3, subparagraph 4 of the Decree (hereinafter referred to as “securities”) in lieu of cash pursuant to statutes or regulations, the cashier shall handle them in the same manner as cash.

Article 112 (Deposit of Cash, Etc.) A cashier shall, without delay, pay cash or securities received (hereinafter referred to as “cash, etc.”) to the Bank of Korea, etc. or deposit them with a financial company, etc. <Amended 2011.10.4>

Article 113 (Restrictions on Custody of Cash, Etc.) A cashier shall not personally keep cash, etc.: Provided, That this shall not apply in any of the following cases: <Amended 2011.10.4>
1. Where a cashier handling receipts or a cashier handling funds for advance use temporarily keeps cash, etc. received before paying it to or depositing it with the Bank of Korea, etc. or a financial company, etc.;
2. Where a cashier handling agency operating expenses keeps cash for cash payments under the proviso to Article 36(1) of the Decree.

Article 114 (Direct Custody of Cash, Etc.) Where a cashier keeps cash, etc. under the proviso to Article 113, the cashier shall keep it in a sturdy container.

Article 115 (Reporting Loss of Cash, Etc.) Where a cashier loses cash, etc. in the cashier's custody, the cashier shall, without delay, submit a report on the loss of cash stating the following matters to the head of the central government agency to which the cashier belongs, through the head of the cashier's agency:
1. Name of the agency to which the cashier belongs;
2. Name and position of the cashier;
3. Date, time and place of the loss;
4. Amount lost;
5. Cause and circumstances of the loss;
6. How the loss was discovered;
7. Measures taken after discovering the loss;
8. Other matters for reference.

Article 116 (Prohibition of Concurrent Duties) The duties of a cashier handling receipts and a cashier handling agency operating expenses shall not be performed concurrently by the same person: Provided, That this shall not apply where, in the case of a fund, there is an unavoidable reason for concurrent performance of those duties due to an insufficient staffing complement.

Article 117 (Procedures for Cashiers' Affairs Other Than Those in These Rules) The head of a central government agency may determine matters concerning procedures for handling the affairs of cashiers belonging to that agency other than those prescribed in these Rules.

CHAPTER IX SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

SECTION 1 RESOLUTIONS, BOOKS AND REPORTS

Article 118 Deleted. <2003.12.31>

Article 119 (Recording and Maintenance of Subsidiary Books)
(1) Public officials engaged in accounting may maintain subsidiary books, in addition to the accounting books under Article 92 of the Decree, where deemed necessary. <Amended 2008.10.1>
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy and the heads of central government agencies shall maintain books in the following forms under Articles 93 and 94 of the Decree and may maintain other subsidiary books where deemed necessary: <Amended 2007.11.6, 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
1. Annual revenue ledger: attached Form No. 22;
2. Annual expenditure ledger: attached Form No. 23;
3. Fund receipts ledger: attached Form No. 24;
4. Fund disbursements ledger: attached Form No. 25;
5. General annual revenue ledger: attached Forms No. 26 and No. 26-2;
6. General annual expenditure ledger: attached Forms No. 27 and No. 27-2.
(3) The date of preparation of subsidiary books under paragraph (1) shall be the date of preparation of the resolutions under Article 123(1). <Amended 2008.10.1>

Article 120 (Restoration of Lost or Destroyed Books, Etc.)
(1) Where accounting books or documents are lost or destroyed due to a natural disaster or other accident, public officials engaged in accounting shall prepare them anew without delay. In such cases, where the amounts in the books cannot be ascertained, the figures may be determined with the approval of the head of the central government agency.
(2) Where accounting documents, such as monthly reconciliation statements under Article 124, supporting documents for receipts, and documents concerning commitments to disburse, are lost, destroyed or damaged, public officials engaged in accounting may request copies and corresponding certification from the institutions that issued the documents, receiving institutions, etc. <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 121 (Preparation and Submission of Reports)
(1) Public officials engaged in accounting shall submit reports in the following forms under Article 97 of the Decree even where there have been no receipts, disbursements or cash resources transactions: <Amended 2007.11.6>
1. Report on revenue collection: attached Form No. 28;
2. Report on amounts of commitments to disburse and amounts disbursed: attached Form No. 29;
3. Deleted. <2007.11.6>
(2) Public officials engaged in accounting shall attach to the reports under paragraph (1) copies of the monthly reconciliation statements for the relevant month, statements of differences under Article 125(1), and other reference documents.

Article 122 (Correction of Reports)
(1) Where, after submitting a report under Article 121, a public official engaged in accounting needs to correct an entry in that report, the official shall make the correction by showing the increase or decrease in the relevant portion of the report for the month to be corrected and append the reason.
(2) Where a correction is necessary after the report for the final month has been submitted, a public official engaged in accounting shall submit, by January 25 of the following fiscal year, a corrected final report showing increases or decreases relative to the report already submitted.

Article 123 (Preparation of Books and Documents Using Information and Communications Media)
(1) Accounting books, resolutions and reports prepared by public officials engaged in accounting shall be prepared using the digital budget and accounting system. <Amended 2007.11.6>
(2) In addition to the forms under paragraph (1), the head of a central government agency may have the subsidiary books under Article 119(1) prepared using information and communications media designated by that head. In such cases, the head shall consult the Minister of Finance and Economy in advance. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) Public officials engaged in accounting shall retain electronically the accounting books, etc. prepared by the methods under paragraphs (1) and (2), and shall maintain and manage information and communications auxiliary storage media containing the relevant data, such as diskettes or magnetic tapes, until the expiry of the retention periods for the relevant accounting books and subsidiary books. <Amended 2008.10.1>

SECTION 2 MONTHLY RECONCILIATION

Article 124 (Monthly Reconciliation)
(1) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall prepare monthly reconciliation statements each month and send them, using the digital budget and accounting system, by the 3rd day of the following month to revenue collection officers, disbursing officers and cashiers (hereinafter in this Section referred to as “revenue collection officers, etc.”).
