Revenue collection officers, etc. shall verify the monthly reconciliation statements sent by the Bank of Korea, etc. using the digital budget and accounting system by the 5th day of the following month. <Amended 2007.11.6>
(2) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. is unable to send monthly reconciliation statements using the digital budget and accounting system, it shall send three copies of each statement by registered mail to the revenue collection officers, etc. by the 3rd day of the following month. The revenue collection officers, etc. shall examine and verify them and return two copies to the Bank of Korea, etc. by the 5th day. <Amended 2007.11.6>
[Wholly amended 2005.6.30]

Article 125 (Method of Monthly Reconciliation)
(1) Revenue collection officers, etc. shall reconcile and verify, using the digital budget and accounting system under Article 124, the figures in monthly reconciliation statements sent by the Bank of Korea, etc. against the figures in resolutions, etc. Where a correction is necessary in that process, they shall append it to the monthly reconciliation statement and prepare a statement of the difference. <Amended 2005.6.30, 2007.11.6>
(2) Where, after verifying a monthly reconciliation statement, a revenue collection officer, etc. discovers an error in its figures, the officer shall send a written statement of the reason to the Bank of Korea, etc. and request a correction. <Amended 2005.6.30>

SECTION 3 CORRECTION OF ERRORS

Article 126 (Requests for Correction of Errors) Where receipts or disbursements have been received or disbursed with the fiscal year, account, responsible agency, etc. entered incorrectly, the public official engaged in accounting shall request the Bank of Korea, etc. to correct the error by January 20 of the following fiscal year. In such cases, the request shall be made by the public official engaged in accounting responsible for the relevant affairs. Where another public official engaged in accounting discovers the error, that official shall inform the responsible public official engaged in accounting so that a correction may be requested. <Amended 2015.11.26>

Article 127 (Correction of Entries in Supporting Documents for Receipts) Where a cashier discovers an error in entries in a notice of supporting documents for receipts or a statement of cash payments, the cashier shall request its correction from the revenue collection officer or the Bank of Korea, etc. by January 20 of the following fiscal year. <Amended 2015.11.26>

Article 128 (Correction of Errors) Where the Bank of Korea, etc. receives from a public official engaged in accounting a request to correct an error under Articles 126 and 127, it shall take the procedures for correction as of the date of receipt and notify that public official engaged in accounting of the result.

Article 129 (Correction of Errors After the Fiscal Year) Where a public official engaged in accounting fails to correct an error within the period for closing receipt and disbursement accounts, the official shall continue accounting for it in its existing state. For an error involving another public official engaged in accounting, however, the official shall notify that other official of the reason and amount.

Article 130 (Adjustment of Accounting Books) Where a public official engaged in accounting, after requesting the Bank of Korea, etc. to correct an error under Articles 126 and 127, receives notice that the correction has been completed, the official shall adjust the accounting books as of that date. In such cases, where the notice of completed correction is received after the month in which the correction was requested, the reason shall be appended to the report for the month in which the notice is received.

SECTION 4 HANDOVER OF AFFAIRS, ETC.

Article 131 (Handover and Taking Over of Affairs)
(1) When a public official engaged in accounting is replaced, the predecessor shall close the accounting books as of the day preceding the replacement date and affix the predecessor's name and seal.
(2) When a public official engaged in accounting is replaced, the following accounting documents shall be prepared and handed over together with a statement of handover and taking over of affairs: <Amended 2011.10.4>
1. Revenue collection officer: receipts collection ledger and subsidiary books, statement of uncollected amounts, certificate of amounts received by the Bank of Korea, and related documents;
2. Finance officer: commitment-to-disburse ledger and subsidiary books, statement of commitments to disburse, and related documents;
3. Disbursing officer: disbursements ledger and subsidiary books, withholding tax ledger, and related documents;
4. Cashier: cash transaction ledger and subsidiary books, certificate of treasury deposit balance (meaning a certificate of the treasury deposit balance as of the day preceding the replacement date requested from and issued by the financial company, etc. with which transactions are conducted), statement of cash on hand, and related documents.
(3) When an officer authorizing transactions in funds for advance use, an officer authorizing transactions in the national funds investment account, or a cashier handling the national funds investment account is replaced, the handover and taking over shall follow the procedures applicable to public officials engaged in accounting under paragraph (2). <Amended 2005.6.30>
(4) The predecessor and successor who have completed the handover and taking over under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall each retain one copy of the handover statement and inventory and submit one copy to the head of the central government agency or the head of the institution to which they belong. <Amended 2005.6.30>

Article 132 (Handover and Taking Over of Cash, Etc.)
(1) When a cashier keeping cash is replaced, the predecessor and successor cashiers shall compare the statement of cash on hand with the cash, hand over and receive the cash, and affix their names and seals to the statement of cash on hand recording that fact.
(2) When a cashier handling agency operating expenses who keeps a treasury deposit passbook is replaced, the predecessor and successor cashiers shall compare the certificate of treasury deposit balance with the balance in the passbook, hand over and receive the passbook, and affix their names and seals to a written statement recording that fact.
(3) When a public official keeping a card is replaced, the predecessor and successor shall compare the card transaction details with the sales slips, hand over and receive them, and affix their names and seals to a written statement recording that fact.

Article 133 (Handover and Taking Over of Affairs by Acting Public Officials Engaged in Accounting, Etc.)
(1) When acting public officials engaged in accounting, public officials separately undertaking part of accounting affairs, etc. under Article 105(2) of the Decree are replaced or appointed, their affairs shall be handed over and taken over in accordance with Articles 131 and 132.
(2) Where a public official engaged in accounting, an acting public official engaged in accounting, a public official separately undertaking part of accounting affairs, etc. cannot hand over affairs due to an accident or other inability, the head of the central government agency shall have another public official make the handover on that official's behalf.

Article 134 (Procedures for Abolishing Accounting Officer Positions, Etc.)
(1) Where the head of a central government agency intends to abolish a position of a public official engaged in accounting, the head shall designate a public official engaged in accounting to take over the remaining affairs of the relevant official, have the affairs handed over and taken over, and notify the Minister of Finance and Economy, the Board of Audit and Inspection, and the Bank of Korea, etc. (limited to cases involving a revenue collection officer) of the fact. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2019.7.1, 2026.1.2>
(2) Where a central government agency is abolished, the head of that agency shall notify the head of the newly responsible central government agency, the Minister of Finance and Economy, the Board of Audit and Inspection, and the Bank of Korea, etc. (limited to cases involving a revenue collection officer) of the status of each public official engaged in accounting belonging to the agency being abolished. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2019.7.1, 2026.1.2>
(3) A public official engaged in accounting whose position is abolished shall close the accounting books and related documents as of the day preceding the abolition and hand over and transfer affairs in accordance with Articles 131 and 132. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2019.7.1>
(4) A cashier handling receipts or funds for advance use whose position is abolished shall pay cash on hand to the revenue collection officer without delay. <Amended 2019.7.1>
(5) A cashier handling agency operating expenses whose position is abolished shall return the treasury deposit passbook and cards in the cashier's custody (meaning all cards kept by their respective holders) to the disbursing officer together with the documents under paragraph (8), and both the cashier and the disbursing officer shall affix their respective names and seals to a statement recording the handover and receipt. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2019.7.1>
(6) Where a cashier handling agency operating expenses returns a treasury deposit passbook and cards under paragraph (5), the cashier shall pay the treasury deposit balance and cash on hand into the National Treasury and apply to the credit card business operator, etc. to terminate use of the cards. In such cases, where any card transactions remain unsettled, the cashier shall pay the balance of the treasury deposit passbook after excluding those amounts. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2017.12.29, 2019.7.1>
(7) In applying paragraphs (5) and (6) to an electronic debit payment means, return of the card shall be replaced by the cashier handling agency operating expenses applying to the credit card business operator, etc. to terminate use of that electronic debit payment means and reporting to the disbursing officer that its use has been terminated. <Newly inserted 2019.7.1>
(8) A public official engaged in accounting whose position is abolished shall submit the following documents, together with the official seal, to the head of the central government agency: <Amended 2019.7.1>
1. Revenue collection officer: final report on amounts of revenue collected, final monthly receipts reconciliation statement of uncollected amounts, and certification of total amounts received by the Bank of Korea;
2. Finance officer: final report on amounts of commitments to disburse and certification of the balance of budget allocations;
3. Disbursing officer: final report on amounts disbursed and certification of amounts disbursed;
4. Cashier: final cash transaction report, final monthly reconciliation statement, certification of treasury deposit balance, certification of cash balance, and certification of card transaction amounts.
(9) Certifications of amounts relating to receipts and disbursements of national funds prescribed in Article 132(2) and (3) and paragraph (8) of this Article shall be requested from and issued by the Bank of Korea, etc., the financial companies, etc. with which transactions are conducted, and the credit card business operators, etc. with which transactions are conducted. <Amended 2008.10.1, 2011.10.4, 2017.12.29, 2019.7.1>

Article 135 (Other Forms) Forms of other accounting books, disbursement- and payment-related documents, and various reports necessary for enforcing the Act, the Decree and these Rules shall be as follows: <Amended 2007.11.6>
1. Cash transaction ledger: attached Form No. 31;
2. Correction statement for commitments to disburse: attached Forms No. 32 and No. 32-2;
3. Adjustment statement for commitments to disburse: attached Forms No. 33 and No. 33-2;
4. Ledger of commitments to pay: attached Form No. 34;
5. Report on collection of receipts: attached Form No. 35;
6. Report on payments of agency operating expenses: attached Form No. 36;
7. Report on collection of receipts for expenses financed by offsetting receipts: attached Form No. 37;
8. Correction statement for disbursement resolutions: attached Forms No. 38 and No. 38-2.
